provenance.operatorDescription: Varies the court applications a register defendant is linked to, to find out whether the unguarded lookup at ProsecutionCaseOrApplicationMapper.js:62-65 can be made to miss.
provenance.operatorRationale: Defect row C20 says the application lookup — `hearingJson.courtApplications.find((ca) => ca.id === applicationId)` with no array guard and no result guard — kills the register on an absent array or an unmatched id, and the fix makes the register survive with the remaining cases. The first audit run found the row explaining nothing, and the obvious remedy — build a hearing with a dangling application reference — turns out to be impossible: the list being iterated and the array being searched are BUILT FROM AND READ FROM THE SAME `courtApplications`. DefendantContextBaseService.js:149 pushes `courtApplication.id` only for applications that passed isEligible, and the mapper then looks that same id up in that same array. So this operator does not manufacture a dangling reference; it MEASURES the coupling that makes one impossible, which is the only honest thing a corpus can do with a guard whose trigger no payload produces. The three variants move the id, remove the eligibility, and add an ineligible application: the invariant to look for in the recordings is that `applications` is always a subset of the ids present, never the reverse, and that every one of these produces a register rather than a swallowed TypeError.

operatorDetail.why: every courtApplication.id is replaced. If the gathering and the lookup read different arrays this would dangle; because they read the same one, both move together and the register is produced exactly as before
